utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Counsel and the parties would be aware that the Chamber insists on punctuality. It's a matter both of courtesy and a matter of efficiency, and -- but notwithstanding the desirability of that, from time to time problems do arise, and in this case the Chamber must apologise for the inconvenience to counsel and the parties for taking the bench a little late. Thank you. Yes, may I have the -- I was about to ask for the appearances, but Ms. Korner, you were on your feet. Were you about to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was about to announce the appearances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. It's Joanna Korner, Crispian Smith for the Prosecution today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Appearing for Stanisic Defence Slobodan Zecevic, Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic to my right and then our case manager Ms. Tatjana Savic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Zupljanin Defence: Igor Pantelic, Mr. Dragan Krgovic, Mr. Brent Hicks, and Mr. Eric Tully. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So noted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's one matter I need to raise before the witness comes into court, which relates to the evidence of the witness. The second matter is I believe Your Honours have been informed about the problem that has arisen with the witness next week through VWS's contact with the witness. I'm not sure how it's going to be resolved at the moment, but it may cause yet again, I'm afraid, a possible gap. Can I say we were unaware of the fact that he couldn't travel, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I believe so. It's the one that VWS contacted Ms. Featherstone about -- Mrs. Featherstone. Your Honours, then in relation to the next witness, he's the first witness that falls into the category that I said something about my opening; namely, he is connected with the events that happened in Kotor Varos, if I can put it that way, from the side of the defendants, accused. Your Honours, it's a matter for Your Honours, but I feel I ought to remind Your Honours of Rule 90(E). I should tell Your Honours that he was interviewed on two occasion by the Office of the Prosecutor as a suspect. So he was given his rights not to answer questions. He did answer questions then, but that was a right that was given to him at the time. So as I say, I think it's really a matter for Your Honours to make the decision as to whether any warning needs to be given and, if so, at what stage, but I thought I'd better remind Your Honours of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Does he fall under the category of witnesses covered by Rule 90 -- yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He's Rule 90(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He comes or it was thought -- or it's a rather odd rule now as -- under the definition of a suspect in Rule 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, so he does not require any protective measures, and so, Your Honours, the next witness is Nedjelko Djekanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Korner and Counsels, I would like to make a request to the parties in relation to the witness statements. Yesterday there was reference across the courtroom to the statements made or given by the previous witness, and Defence counsels raised at several occasions the statements and confronted the earlier statements to the witness directly, and the Prosecution in return sought also to rebut the evidence offered by the witness in response to the challenge made by the Defence counsels arising out of his earlier statement. For this reason, I would like to ask the parties to in the future to submit also the earlier statements to the Chamber as they're being exchanged to the other party.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that in relation -- in relation just to the 92 ter witnesses or to viva voce witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm fully aware of the controversial aspect of this request, but my request would be for both, both for viva voce and for 92 ter witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, may I say in my last trial here certainly the Judges had copies particularly of these interviews. I think we're perfectly prepared to supply them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Korner. Thank you, Counsels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: At yesterday's adjournment counsel would recall that I had indicated there was a possibility of us sitting on Thursday and Friday in the mornings. We can now confirm that we would be sitting tomorrow morning and Friday morning, and I'm giving this early heads-up so that counsel can arrange their affairs accordingly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may please address the Chamber in relation to your announcement of times of sitting for tomorrow. I really kindly ask you. This is a very unique situation that we have here today given the importance of this witness for the Defence, and then if possible in future if we have similar situation then to have possibility to -- not to jump from the evening session to the morning, because we have to prepare cross-examination, to check many documents. I agree ruling is absolutely accepted, but just to have in mind that in specific situation when we have very serious questions -- sorry, witnesses for the Defence that that should be taken in mind. Thank you so much in advance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. Good afternoon, sir. Thank you for your appearance here this afternoon. The -- what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nedjelko Djekanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 15th of November, 1958.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And -- and what is your ethnicity, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Have you testified previously in this -- in these proceedings, the proceedings of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not before this Tribunal but before some other court organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [overlapping speakers] ... Sorry, my microphone may have been off. What is your profession or occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a mechanical engineer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Korner, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, let me start by setting the background to how you come to be here as a witness. I think it's right that you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The first on the 12th of June of 2003.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And secondly, on the 25th of March of this year.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before speaking to the Office of the Prosecutor in March of this year, I think it's right that you spoke to or had an interview with the Defence for Stojan Zupljanin in this case, in particular Mr. Pantelic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you've had an opportunity to speak to the Defence since your arrival in The Hague. Can I ask, did you speak to them last night or this morning?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: We met last night over a cup of coffee.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And finally, I think it's right that you are testifying here not voluntarily but because a summons was issued by this court which you are obeying.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've been asked for your occupation presently. Can I deal with your past occupations. I think at the time of the multi-party elections in 1990, were you a member of the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the SDS then as I am now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as a member of that party, did you stand for election to the Assembly of, as it was then, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a candidate for the municipal assembly of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I won at the first multi-party elections, and I became a deputy representing the municipality of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So is that what's called the Chamber of the Municipalities of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you were elected, is this right, for -- to the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was also a deputy to the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I want to ask you, please, a little bit, first of all, about Kotor Varos. Firstly, I think it was pretty evenly ethnically divided; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Kotor Varos municipality had around 36.000 inhabitants. According to the census of 1991, Serbs comprised over 36 per cent of that population, nearly 14.000. Muslims had slightly over 10.000 inhabitants, and Croats were somewhat less, 9.000 plus. In such an ethnic make-up when everyone voted for the Assembly as an SDS representative and a Serb, I won in the second round of elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dealing with what happened after those elections as regards positions in the Assembly and elsewhere, did Ante (sic) Mandic of the HDZ, the Croat party, become the president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Anto Mandic did become the president of the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos, but after an agreement had been reached with the SDS and at the level of the three parties' leadership, it was agreed that at local levels the party which received the most votes can appoint their own person at -- at the position of the Municipal Assembly president. In Kotor Varos the SDS was that party, and pursuant to the agreement we could appoint the Assembly president. In agreement with the HDZ, we agreed that they appoint a person to that position. The person was Anto Mandic. We as the SDS took the second position that had originally been allocated to the HDZ, to the Croats, that is to say, and that person was supposed to be the deputy president Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. You, however, did you not, took the position of chairman of the Executive Committee of the Assembly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as you've pointed out because you in fact got more votes in the election, you could have had the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly. Why did you decide to take the Executive Committee?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: We couldn't have both the president of the Assembly and the President of the Executive Board. We were allowed to appoint a person to the post of the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly, but in agreement with the Croats we swapped the two places, and actually it was Momcilo Komljenovic who came President of the Executive Board, not myself. The reasons were that we were of the opinion, politically speaking, that it was favourable for us to have a President of the Executive Board from amongst our ranks, because that person was in charge of many programmes such as development in Kotor Varos. Such programmes were mainly discussed at the Executive Board, and that is why we decided to opt for that position. That decision was not unanimously agreed upon in -- by the SDS. It was simply a majority vote that decided.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. In the light of the composition of the -- of the three parties, which I think reflected the -- as it were, the ethnic make-up, did the SDS have an absolute majority in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No party had an absolute majority. The SDS had only a relative majority.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it follows from that that if the SDS and the HDZ decided to band together, they could out-vote the SDS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: If we are to look into the statute and decisions of the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos, such options were not included. But if we go by the simple number of votes, then they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then as far as the SDS is concerned, were you in fact president of the municipal SDS board in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the time of the multi-party elections but shortly afterwards. I believe as of February or January. I cannot recall precisely. It was then that I took charge of the SDS board in Kotor Varos. Later on, I was also president of the municipal SDS board of the Kotor Varos as well as several -- I took up several other positions in the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did that Presidency within the Municipal Board give you a seat on the Regional Board of the SDS based in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not recall whether automatically all municipal SDS presidents became members of the Regional Board. I tend not to think that way, but in any case, I frequently participated at Regional Board meetings of the SDS, including some other party members from Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that Regional Board presided over by somebody called Dr. Vukic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Chronologically speaking, I cannot recall the persons who occupied that position. There were several of them, and I don't know in what term they came, but I think for a while Dr. Vukic was the president of the SDS Regional Board.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, at this stage in 1991, were you a member of the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you later become a member of the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I became a member of the Main Board of the party in 1996, 1997, or 1998. At any case, during that period and not during the period that you are asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you in a moment a few more questions about how the structure of the SDS worked, but can I ask you now to look at some photographs and maps which relate to Kotor Varos, and let's deal with that at this stage. First of all, could you have a look at a map which shows the very ethnic breakdown, which is 65 ter number 10117. I think you had a opportunity to look at this yesterday when you went through a bundle of documents. Can you just tell us, we can see there the, as it were, the majority nationality is shown for each of these villages. Do you accept that's an accurate map?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in? Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, do you want to suggest that there's -- if you think there are some aspects which are not correct, then do tell us, sir.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: You cannot depict such a diverse ethnic make-up on a single map in Kotor Varos. There were villages which were mixed, and yet here they are shown as single ethnicity villages, although there was significant populations of other ethnicities there. Generally speaking, this was so. That is not in dispute. The town of Kotor Varos itself had a Serb majority.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. As I say, sir, I accept entirely that even in villages which are marked as Muslim ones there were other ethnicities living there. Actually, I don't need to bother about the next map. Could you have a look, please, at --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I -- I'm not sure we've made this an exhibit. No, we haven't. Could I ask that be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Entered -- marked and entered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P65, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next, can I ask that you have a look, please, at 65 ter number 03158. Now, sir, you had a chance to look at this yesterday, and indeed I think you -- from the original one that you looked at, you made some corrections because you said that the sawmill had been put in the wrong place. Can you confirm now that the photographs of the various buildings are shown in the right place on the map?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: It seems to me that the SJB building, that is to say the police building, is not in the proper location. The hospital is more or less positioned well. Between the Catholic church and the hospital it is there that the police building should be. On a map we saw yesterday, we can see that clearly, and I believe we marked it as such. The last facility on the right-hand side, although I don't have translation here, is something that I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, it's said to be the Kotor Varos prison, or a building that was used as a prison.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: That is possible, next to the court. In terms of physical location this could be it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, can I -- you say that the SJB building should be between what, the hospital -- the Catholic church and the --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is now and it was so. It's still in the same location.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. So it should be between the Catholic church and where the hospital is shown, but on the main road; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the main road. Somewhat closer to the hospital than to the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And can you just, because it's not indicated here, could you tell us where the municipal building was, where the Municipal Assembly sat?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly building is further away from the court and the prison you marked here. It is further down on this map by a few hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you mean it's not shown on the map at all?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right. Actually, it cannot be placed here on this part of the map that we can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. So it's further down from where we've indicated the prison. That's what you're saying, is it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a bit lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, do you think the witness can actually mark with a pencil.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I don't. Can he? I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think so. It would be useful to see exactly where the prison is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Apparently he can mark on the board.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Could you tell us by putting a small circle and a "P" where the prison is according to your -- to your observation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in the correct place, the prison. It would be more or less here. The prison is in the correct position, because I determined the location of the municipality on the basis of the location of the prison. So here I think it is in the proper place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you put a small "P" to indicate this is the -- sorry, SJB, could you just write "SJB" next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- sorry. The distance between the SJB building and the municipal building was how much, because maps can sometimes be deceptive.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: In my estimate it would be some 800 metres. Perhaps it could be a hundred metres up or down, but it's about 800 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's -- that's all I'm going to ask you. I may ask you to look at some photographs at some other stage, because we've got some new photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. While we're on the same topic, maybe it would be appropriate the witness mark sawmill, because I think he mentioned that it was not the right position on the map so maybe we could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, this is the corrected version. He mentioned that yesterday and we corrected it. I'll get --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, could you confirm that is where the sawmill is -- was, in certainly 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: It's more or less in the same place. The sawmill was opposite from the Catholic church, across the street from the Catholic church. To the right side on the exit road from Kotor Varos towards Banja Luka was the Catholic church, and then on the opposite side of the road is the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So -- yes. I think what you were being asked to confirm is that it's shown correctly on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you wish --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P66, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just one clarification, Your Honours. In a previous case -- this is just one comment. In a previous case, we would have a problem with -- with the documents which were marked by the witness, and they have been given an IT number in order to not to mix with the original document which is tendered by the Prosecution, which, for example, is a map of Kotor Varos, P66. So I'm just suggesting that anyway we just -- we just give it some -- some kind of indication that this is a map which the witness has drawn upon. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you are absolutely right, and I guess the Court was simply not quick enough on its feet to -- to make an observation about this. In general terms, I think the Court would prefer not to have pre-marked maps being presented in court unless it's for -- for other purpose, but in instances like this where the witness is being shown a map and could you please point out where this or that is, I think it's the safest to ask him to do so in court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, just so I follow. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours, but still when the witness like in this case has marked the map in the court, it is my understanding of the e-court that the -- that the photo is taken of that particular document where there is his markings where -- which he just shown to us like SJB. There is a photo made and it's downloaded in a memory. That is my understanding. So this document is somewhat different than the original P66 which was given by the OTP, and I -- and it is my understanding that such documents where the witness marks them are given an IC number, IC number. Well, that was -- that was the case in our previous case, and that was the explanation we were given during the -- during the e-court training.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I'm just -- better clarify this right now. I overheard what you were discussing. I'm sorry, but it was heard over here. Now, I understand our P66 is a marked map. Okay. The situation might be the following: One -- the witness which is -- which is proposed by the Prosecution does not mark. He recognises the map. He says it's okay. Now, I call -- I call that particular document during my cross-examination, and then I show him, let's say P66, and then he draws on the map. So what -- and I ask that document to be tendered. What are we going to do then? I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I think if you want somebody else to put another drawing on the original map, then you just call up the document and you ask your witness to put on it whatever he wants to put. So then that becomes a new Exhibit. P66 is now this map with this witness's marking. The original map has not been tendered into evidence, and it doesn't need to be, for all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, please -- I beg you to bear with me. It might be the situation where the actual position of the CJB (sic) might be an issue. It might be an issue. It might be the situation where this witness will show where in his opinion or his recollection the CJB was, and the other witness might say it was cross the river. Now, if I show the next witness which comes and he says the CJB was across the river, of course it doesn't make sense that I show him the -- the map which was marked by this witness. It should be the original map we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Okay. I think we're talking past each other. The map as you see it on the screen now has not been tendered into evidence. It lies as a document that can be pulled up at any time in the form and shape it has just now. Now, if you have a witness and there is another witness and there's disagreement about where the SJB building was, then you can confront your witness with this witness's marking and you can tell him that, you know, another witness claimed it was here. Then you revert to the original map, and you ask your witness then to indicate where he thinks or she thinks the SJB building was, and then in the end we can sit with two maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I just thought that it -- this, what I was proposing, was much simpler to deal with, but if Your Honours please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As you know, I mean, this system is new to me since I was last here, but the way we dealt with it, and it seems sensible, what we want exhibited is an original unmarked map so we can pull that up at any time, and then our suggestion would have been that this is marked, the map -- the copy that's being marked by this witness is P60, whatever it is, .1. So at least we know that's what it is and it reflects on the transcript and it's quite simple, and I see both sides nodding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We fully agree with -- this is exactly what I was talking about. Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: To complete the confusion, we are now being instructed or told or advised by the registry that this is -- what we have just agreed on is in fact impractical. The 65 ter exhibit that you had showing the witness's pre-markings should remain as such. It has not been admitted into evidence, but it remains a 65 ter number. Now, if anyone wishes to use the same map unmarked, that is to say without the witness's pre-markings, which is to go back to the very original version of this document before the witness actually marked it out, then that should be given a 65 ter number so that the Defence can use the raw original version of the map for any subsequent purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I still --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Got it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to say perhaps, Your Honour, we can try and sort this out maybe at the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Mr. Djekanovic, we'll leave for the moment what Kotor Varos look like. Can I ask you next about your knowledge of the two accused. Firstly, you told us you were a member of the Assembly, the Chamber of Municipalities in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did you then subsequently become a deputy to the -- the Assembly, as it was then called, of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As such, did you ever meet Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I met Mico Stanisic during the Assembly sessions. We didn't have any private or official contacts other than that. I knew him as a man who worked on the same tasks and in similar organs that I did, but we didn't have any other contacts or things in common.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And which organs did he work on that -- that you did? Or which tasks, sorry, first of all?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: He worked in the MUP organs. I don't know what all the posts he had were. I really cannot remember after all this time. Many people and a lot of time has passed since then, so I don't know exactly which posts he was serving in. I think for a time he was perhaps a minister as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about your answer. "I knew him as a man who worked on the same tasks." I was just asking you what tasks.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the government and ministers attended the Assembly sessions of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But you say you didn't have any private contacts or -- or official contacts other than in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's turn to Stojan Zupljanin. When did you first meet him?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I met Stojan Zupljanin after the first multi-party elections in 1990. That was the first time that I met him. I didn't know him before then. It's true that Stojan is from our municipality, but he was a man who worked in the MUP structures, and before he had worked in Banja Luka, so I didn't have the opportunity to get to know him before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how did you come to meet him after the first multi-party elections?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: We first met during the process of the elections during the candidacy process for the chief of the CSB in Banja Luka. That's when we met. And members of all the Municipal Boards from all the municipalities put forward their candidate. So we were happy that a person who is from our municipality was also put forward as a candidate. So he did have our support and the support of other municipalities for the post of chief of the public security centre in Banja Luka, the CSB in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you were supporting him as chief of the CSB. What qualities, in your view, did he possess to become chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't the only one who offered my support. He had the support of the entire party in the Kotor Varos region, all the people from our party from Kotor Varos. To tell the truth, we didn't even discuss any abilities or at the time, at any structure level, not just within the SDS but within any political party, the criteria was not based on abilities or aptitude. It was just the time that had dictated that certain people be elected to certain positions. Ultimately we were there from the beginning, and he was working on these police jobs anyway, so it was natural that he was an educated man. He had worked through those structures and was familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But you said that a number of Municipal Boards were putting forward candidates for this position. So you voted for him, is that what you're saying, simply because he came from Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: One of the main reasons was that he was our candidate, just like others put other candidates forward because they were closer to them, although there were some other reasons too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what were the other reasons?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I said that there were no other reasons --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No other reasons.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: -- due to which we --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Between that election which I think was May of 1991 and June of 1992, how often did you see Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Now after so much time has passed I cannot really say how frequently we saw each other. I mean, we did see each other. We did run into each other, but I really couldn't say how often that was. Just by the nature of our work. There was no need for us to really meet, but we did meet often during 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to deal with some of the events where you came across him in a moment. Can I next ask you, as I said I would, about SDS and their policies. Who formulated the policies for the S --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just one correction for the transcript. The witness just said "we didn't met often during 1992," and the transcript, page 22, line 4, it says "we did met."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But that's what I heard over the translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll repeat the question. Between the elections and -- the election of Stojan Zupljanin as chief of the CSB and June of 1992, did you say that you met him often in 1992 or not often?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Not often. It was the nature of our work that we didn't really need to meet often. We were not working on the same tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then I'll come back to the SDS. I was asking you, please, who formulated SDS policy?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Who was it -- you've told us about a Main Board, a Regional Board, and the Municipal Boards of the SDS. If there was a policy to be followed, who would decide what that policy was? Would it be the Main Board or the Regional Board or the Municipal Board?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Depending on the level. The policy and the procedure of adopting decisions is regulated by the statute of the party, so every level of the party had its own statute. The municipal, regional, and the republican structures or the SDS top leadership had those. So depending on the level, the policy of the party was adopted pursuant to the statutory norms at the party organs. And pursuant to who had lesser or a greater influence in the adoption of these decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's -- let's start with the stop. If the Main Board of the SDS made a decision, was it the obligation under the statute for that decision to be put into effect by the Regional Board and then the Municipal Board?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: If possible, yes, but in many cases there were many exceptions where literally some decision which was of a general nature could not be applied at all levels and in all areas. There was some instances like that in our region of Kotor Varos as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps you can just to illustrate give us one example of where the Main Board made the decision which you couldn't put into effect in the Kotor Varos region.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: The first decision was the election of the president of the municipality. The position of the negotiating team of the SDS that reached an agreement with the SDA and the HDZ, according to the majority votes, was not implemented. There was a different decision that was actually implemented. Our position was the one that took prevalence. There was another item where the three national parties were deadlocked, and we could not find a solution on this matter, so we had to negotiate in Sarajevo and make new negotiations and look for new resolutions at a higher level, even split up certain departments in order to satisfy all these needs, and this is how we resolved that particular matter. Usually it just depended from case to case how this was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But you're saying here, are you - I just want to make sure that we've all understood - that you couldn't -- when you were deadlocked in your municipality, you had to go back to Sarajevo, to the main boards of all three parties to renegotiate. Is that what you're saying? I just want to make sure we've understood this.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have to go, but the common mutual agreement at the level of the municipality was to try to restructure the composition of power and in that way try to achieve a solution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think we're slightly drifting away. So you're saying there were two -- at least two matters --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have an intervention in the transcript. I believe the witness said that they have reached the common mutual agreement at the level of municipality to ask the three parties in Sarajevo to -- to deal with this situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's what I understood him to be -- to be saying as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that is what you're saying, is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. So does it come to this: You had a certain amount of autonomy within the Municipal Board, but for major matters you had to go back to the Main Board in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Each Municipal Board had a rather comprehensive autonomy in its work, as well as the understanding on the part of the party leadership. The situation on the ground was quite specific, and not all principles could be applied across the board in all municipalities. There were many elements which required separate approaches, and for such problems there was always understanding for in the Main Board of the party. And in several other instances and periods, you can see for yourself that the decisions made by the local party boards were those that were later adopted. I don't think I can say that there were tensions or conflicts along those lines. In any case, the Main Board always took into account local opinions even though such opinions may have been contrary to the policies of the party or the opinions of those in the leadership.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you say it took into account local opinion. Are you saying that as a result of local opinion, the decision, if it was -- I'm sorry. If it was contrary to a policy, then the policy would be changed?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: At the local level there were no key or important decisions which would deviate significantly from the policy of the party. But on the other hand, the policy did not strictly limit or try to impose hierarchical solutions so as to have every single word of the president implemented. I can say with full responsibility that in my political career, sometimes my positions were such that would oppose the rest of the party, and I know that such opinion existed in certain local boards of the party. Even today you meet such situations in the work of the various political parties across Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think we're going to look at one particular document in a moment. Can I next turn to the topic of regionalisation. Was that, in fact, a policy that was adopted by the SDS to begin with?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: If you want me to be honest, the SDS always stood against regionalisation. SDS policy was not regionalisation but, rather, an attempt at centralisation. Although, I must say again that all separate needs were taken into account for regional organisations. During a certain period the regional boards were even abolished and then again reinstated and mentioned in the statute. So the situation changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to ask you to look, please, at a document which is 65 ter number 5, please. And can we -- which you had a chance to look at yesterday. Is that headed "Agreement on the Formation of a Community of Bosnian Krajina Municipalities," and it does it show the municipalities, including Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says. But it is important to say, mentioning this document, that the community of Bosnian Krajina municipalities had existed as part of the SFRY, as well as Republika Srpska. That community had existed even prior to World War II. Kotor Varos, by virtue of its natural geographical position and other historical, cultural, traffic and developmental elements gravitated towards Banja Luka, and it was always a part of that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but the -- you're not saying -- this was a different type of organisation, wasn't it, Mr. Djekanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you have in mind specifically in what way was it different. But there must have been a number of municipalities which were new to such a community. If we compare its statutory role in the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the current status, we would see that the similarities are great. Of course, certain municipalities did not used to belong to the community, but that is not the case with Kotor Varos [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The difference was this -- between this and the one you've just mentioned is this was in fact made up entirely, wasn't it, or almost entirely of Serb --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, another intervention in the transcript. 27, 8, the witness said Kotor Varos was always within this community of the municipalities. Thank you very much. This was left out from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we go back to -- can I have the document back again. All right. The delegates to this association were, if not a hundred per cent, pretty much Serb delegates, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not deny that it was so in that period of time, but that policy existed across all levels, regions, and environments. Here we had Serbs. In some other locations we had Croats and Muslims jointly, and no one was bothered by that when they made decisions, although in the statute and the constitution of the then Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it clearly stated that a decision on the part of one people would not be accepted as valid. Although at certain point they -- this was accepted. Of course, in this environment, Serbs were the only delegates because others refused to participate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why did others refuse to participate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Because they had the concept of centralisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, what we can see now in which one or two peoples would have power over a third. Those people tried to create ties between communities which had never lived together. We had the case of Ante Kotormanovic [as interpreted] who signed a decision that was made public. That decision had to do with the signing of Kotor Varos with the association of the municipality of Herceg-Bosna. This was, I believe, in the spring and it was done without the support of any Serb delegates. This was simply the situation on all three sides at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this was a -- leaving aside Herceg-Bosna -- and I'm not seeking to argue --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Please, just a correction to the transcript. It's at page 28, line 10 and 9. Correct name should be Ante Mandic was at that time president of Kotor Varos municipality. Yes, and that was the association of municipality of Herceg-Bosna, another correction in line 11 and 12. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This association of Bosnian Krajina municipalities transformed itself, didn't it, into something called the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, not it's possible. You attended meetings, didn't you Mr. Djekanovic, of both the association and the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we look, please, at a second document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask that this be admitted now as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P67, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move now, please, to a document which is a list of delegates, which is 65 ter 3107, please. Could we have the English up as well, please. English? Anybody? All right. There's a problem, apparently, with the English. Could we -- if we go in -- because we've got numbers even though it's in Cyrillic, to 172, 173, and 174. It's on page 4 of the document. Right. Next page, please, page 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is 172, sir, Momcilo Komljenovic, from Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he's the gentleman who you told us became head of the Executive Committee of the Municipal Assembly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. After the multi-party elections in 1990, he became president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Goran Krzic, who was he? Who is number 173?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what period this is, but at that time he was the president of the municipal SDS and the president of the Municipal Assembly of Kotor Varos elected at the elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Savo Tepic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Also he was the deputy appointed as the chief of the police station in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And can you tell us why the police chief from Kotor Varos would be attending the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: If you tell me the precise dates -- date of this document and if I could recall things so well 17 years later, I would tell you that I presume that he was not there as the chief of police of the Kotor Varos municipality but as the president of the local SDS board. Perhaps I could not attend. Perhaps I was at the time attending a session of the Republika Srpska Assembly at Pale. That is possible, but in terms of date I cannot recall exactly. I'm not sure -- I am sure he was not there in his capacity as the chief of the police station in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I can't -- I'm afraid I can't assist with the date because it's not a dated document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that now be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. And -- admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And it is now time for the break. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- Recess taken at 3.47 p.m. -- On resuming at 4.09 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Djekanovic, just before we leave the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, the president of that Assembly was somebody called Vojo Kupresanin. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. He was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry? He was. Oh, I see. And the vice --

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the vice-president was Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the entire structure, whether there was an executive body of sorts, but in any case, Radoslav Brdjanin was the man number two.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And as we'll hear, when it came to the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which came out of the Assembly, it was Radoslav Brdjanin who became the president of the Crisis Staff, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: From this seat here it's difficult for me to recall all the details. I know he was the president of the Crisis Staff of the Krajina. I only don't know whether it was throughout the entire period the Crisis Staff existed or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And you knew both Kupresanin and Brdjanin, didn't you, because they were, like you, members of the Assembly of the -- I'm going to call it the Republika Srpska. I know it didn't change its name till much later, but they were both members of the Republika Srpska Assembly, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I want to move now, please, to the events which led to the -- effectively the -- first of all, the declaration of the Serbian Assembly. Were you present at the meeting in October of 1991 of the Bosnia Assembly, the socialist Republic of Bosnia, when the SDS deputies walked out?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you present at the founding session of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, let's look, please, at what happened at the end of 1991. In December of 1991, did you receive a copy of a set of instructions which had been issued by the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can I have, please, 65 ter 2333.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's a document entitled "SDS Main Board." The one we've got is "strictly confidential," copy number 93, "Instructions for the organisation and operation of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in emergency conditions." Did you get a copy of those instructions? And when I say you, not particularly you personally, but you the SDS party in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I have to say that we did have access to that document. At what stage -- during what period of time we actually were able to access it is something I cannot tell you, but I would kindly ask the Chamber to allow me to add something to the last two responses which I believe are important. It has to do with things which preceded this decision of the Serb representatives to form a separate Assembly, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've asked Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's up to Your Honours to allow him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Inasmuch as he's being led by counsel, counsel would know what their respective cases are and we'll see where we go. If the Chamber wishes clarification at the appropriate stage, it would do that, but there's always a reluctance of witnesses to volunteer testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I say straightaway I have no idea what he wants to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Hence the general reluctance to have witnesses volunteer, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it's not exactly my witness in the way that one would normally say it's my witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, sir, we have limited time, but if there's something you feel is important that the Trial Chamber should know, then could you tell them very briefly.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, its's very important for one to know. This decision by the Serb deputies to walk out of the Assembly and form a separate Assembly is something that was preceded by a vote that was taken without the consent of the Serb deputies in the Bosnia-Herzegovina Assembly on the declaration of independence. We were out-voted in spite of all the existing Assembly regulation. That is why we walked out and decided to form a separate Assembly. We realised that even decisions that were supposed to be in force could be simply declared null and void or out-voted. Although that was unconstitutional under the then constitution, we then decided to make this move. This is what I wanted to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What was the issue? Was that the fundamental issue of regionalisation versus centralisation? Was that the issue in which you felt that you were voted down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The issue was the break-up of the former common state of Yugoslavia in which we all lived together. We disagreed with that concept. The SDS and the Serb people at that time had the idea of conserving Yugoslavia and that the Serb people should remain within Yugoslavia. The other two peoples had their own policy. That was to say that Yugoslavia ought to be broken up. Frequently they invoked decisions which were not made in keeping with the then regulation and laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You were asked, sir, whether this had anything to do with regionalisation, because you told us that regionalisation wasn't a policy of the SDS. So can I just ask one further question on that: Are you aware of documents produced by Karadzic and others showing that regionalisation was a policy?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Through my political activity in the SDS and its political bodies, I know that for the most part there were cases in which regionalisation was prevented, because it was widely believed that this would divide or break up the SDS and that local antagonisms would take precedence over the general needs of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As I say, I don't want to be buried in this topic, but were you aware of the declaration of the so-called autonomous regions, including that of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I would also like to say that we didn't really deal with that question too much, because the political side was quite organised in -- in that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, as I say, I've got a lot to get through with you, Mr. Djekanovic, and the Chamber will hear other evidence about this, so I want to move, please, back to this document. You said you had access this document. Do you mean you got the document, because if so, could you say so, please?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot affirmatively answer whether I received this document personally, whether it came through the autonomous region of the Krajina or through the -- the party organs into the party. I really cannot remember at this point how I got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right, but -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there is another -- I'm sorry to interrupt, but there is another problem with the transcript. Page 34, 25, and 35, 1 and 2. I believe the witness said, "I would also like to say that we didn't really deal with that question too much because the Kotor Varos was already a part of regional association of the municipality Bosanska Krajina," and that is not what the -- what the transcript says. Something different. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's not at all what the transcript says. But is that what you said, sir? Because it's not what I heard through my headphones either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. However you got it, you got a copy of this document, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: We did have it at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And that was a set of instructions, wasn't it, from the SDS board for what was to happen. If you turn -- if we go to page 2 of the document. In paragraph 1, it was to implement, as it was put, the decision adopted in the plebiscite by the Serbian people. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the plebiscite referred to, is that the one that was held at the beginning of November of 1991 as to whether Serbs wished to remain in the Yugoslav state?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: The only plebiscite which we conducted was the support to remain in the former state of Yugoslavia. So that is that document. That is that assertion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, the question was whether that's the one that was held at the beginning of November 1991.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I have to stress I don't know what time that -- I really cannot remember after such a long time has passed and in view of the conditions that I'm living in exactly what happened when. If you wished me to state in the order of things that they happened in, I would not be able to do that. When the plebiscite was held, it was during the time when the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina already decided to declare independence regardless of what the Serbian people wished. So it was probably at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's not bother then. Can you -- if we go down the page to paragraph 3: "The tasks, measures and other activities set forth in these instructions shall be implemented over the entire territory of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or in every municipality where the Serbian people live, as follows: "In their entirety in those municipalities where the Serbian people constitute a majority ... "And partially in those municipalities where the Serbian people do not constitute a majority (Variant B)." Which variant did Kotor Varos come -- under which variant did Kotor Varos come?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Kotor Varos had a relative majority Serbian population. I don't know which variant applied where. In seeking a resolution and having this document, which was not an executive document or of the nature of an order, its task was to anticipate or prevent certain things, we were trying to find a solution for survival. So I don't know whether that was the best solution or not, but we did not opt for either Variant A or Variant B in our municipality. We were trying to see what was realistically possible to undertake in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. You say this was not -- I'm sorry. It was not the nature of an order. What do you read the words as, "shall be implemented" as if not an order?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: What will be implemented will be what would be possible to implement and what the situation in the field ensures would be implementable. You have a general assertion here of municipalities where the Serbian population is not in a majority, but nowhere is it explicitly stated exactly what would be implemented in such a situation. So everything that was implemented in Kotor Varos, in my opinion, I'm really unable to see under which variant you would be able to classify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Forget -- forget which variant you were -- I'm sorry. Forget which variant you were for the moment. All I'm asking you is do not the words, "shall be implemented" constitute an order? Whether you could implement it or not is another matter, but isn't that an order?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I spent a long time in the municipality and in politics in those periods, and I never received a document which I strictly had to implement from the SDS. I always carried out a discussion at the party organs, at the Municipal Board. We would always review these matters. Thank God taking into account the policies of the SDS and seeking solutions which for us would be the best, the most acceptable at a given moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I think I'll just ask one more time. Do the words "shall be implemented" mean that it's an order or not? That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I haven't heard an intervention from the other side --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's a leading question. I mean, this is not cross-examination, Your Honour. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said, I'm simply trying to get an answer. I'm not cross-examining him. I'm just asking him to give me an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand that, but the -- as Mr. Krgovic has said, the one point that could be taken as a question has been asked and answered, but I was -- it seemed to me sitting here that one of the difficulties is that you are pressing the witness on the imperative meaning of a word in English, and English -- which may not convey the same meaning in its original form, and perhaps the question should be rephrased. Not saying Mr. Krgovic -- so the question may not have been asked and answered, that you rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I will read the English translation of those words that appear at -- in the first line of paragraph 3 on that page, and I want you to confirm whether it is correct in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's quite difficult to do this actually, Your Honour, but anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "The tasks, measures, and other activities set forth in these instructions shall be implemented ..."

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the Serbian it says: "The tasks, measures, and other activities set forth in these instructions shall be implemented." It does not say -- "are to be implemented."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's note that the distinctions are very, very fine. It's very difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Anyhow I've made my point. We'll move on because we're spending too much time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may try to be of assistance. I think the proper -- maybe the proper English translation would be "carried out."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The word "shall" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: "Would be carried out."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Zecevic, but I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we look, sir, please, then, at what those instructions were, and you say you don't know which variant you came under, but as you told us already, the Croats and Muslims, if they got together, had a larger majority than that of the Serbs, did they not?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were in a majority, but also it was clear that they had already had their own Crisis Staffs, that units were already formed, that practically in a small municipality three armies were practically functioning, three completely opposed to each other military formation. So it was quite normal --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Look, sir, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I do have a limited amount of time. That's not the question I asked you. The simple answer was yes. Those details I'm sure you'll be asked about in cross-examination. For the moment, can we move along and just deal with what you are told to do, putting it neutrally, I hope in this document. If you look at Variant B, which would be my suggestion was the level -- the variant under which you came, at page 7 in the English. And I can probably tell you what it is in the B/C/S as well. It's the same page, I think. All right. Under item 3: "SDS Municipal Boards shall establish immediately a Crisis Staff of the Serbian people in the municipality ..." And then it gives a list of who should be on that Crisis Staff. Did you form a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did form a Crisis Staff, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The president of the SDS Municipal Board shall be the commander of the Crisis Staff." That was you, wasn't it, in Kotor Varos, and did you become, in fact -- I don't think "commander" is the right word, but president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm hearing for the first time that I was the commander of anything, but I was the president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Forget -- I think that's a bad translation. Did you appoint anybody to be a coordinator for relations with the SDA and the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: The coordination with the SDA and the HDZ was present up until almost the end of May 1992, and this coordination proceeded at the level of the president of the SDS Municipal Board or the parties, but mostly at the level of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly where representative of all three parties were. Personally, we co-operated with the president of the municipality and the president of the HDZ. We communicated very well. We sat down often together. We socialised together. We often got drunk together, and we used these occasions to speak. So these communication occurred on a daily basis. We would go to him to his office, he would come to us to our office, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. The question was simply --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Again, I really apologise to my learned friend Ms. Korner. I think on page 41, line 21, I don't think that -- that this witness said, "we often got drunk together." I mean, it's a little bit harsh word, I think. Maybe socialised --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Pantelic -- no, no, Mr. Pantelic, let's not have you giving evidence. Nor do I think it's going to be the most important aspect of this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, but, however, can I urge you, please, to simply answer my questions as shortly as possible. I have a limited amount of time that I have to take you through this, and all that required was, "Yes, there was coordination." Right. Item number 4: "Convene and proclaim an Assembly of a Serbian People in the municipality composed of Assembly men, representatives of the Serbian people in the municipal Assembly, and presidents of SDS local boards." Simple question. Did you actually convene an Assembly of the Serbian People in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did convene it. An Assembly of the Serbian People of the municipality of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which was separate from the elected Municipal Assembly which contained SDA, HDZ, and SDS?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: All political groups and all three national parties had separate parallel structures in the area of the Kotor Varos municipality, including my own -- or, rather, the political structure to which I belonged, the SDS. What we had and what we managed to maintain together continued somehow until May, and that was the Municipal Assembly of the municipality of Kotor Varos, but the first, second, and third of those parties, all of us, were working on other things along parallel tracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Again, sir, whatever the other parties were doing at the moment, I'm simply asking you what you did as a result of the instructions. Right. Item number -- could you turn over -- could we have the next page and see item number 8 -- 7 first. The next page of the document. Item number 7: "Step up information and propaganda in order to ensure that the Serbian people are informed fully and in time ..." Did you carry out that instruction?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: We never had a service or a team of people within the party dealing with any propaganda activities. We did issue a bulletin and the odd proclamation. If you can consider that to be of that nature, then that would be that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you carry out instruction number 8, "Prepare an estimate of the number of necessary active and reserve policemen, TO units ... and bring them up to full manpower levels ..." et cetera?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: That was an item that was impossible to implement, and we did not deal with that at the party organs. We were unable to man or staff any unit or any organ, and we could not implement that in the territory of the Kotor Varos municipality. Therefore, my answer would be no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It says "prepare an estimate." Did you ever give the Main Board an estimate of how many active and reserve policemen and TO units you had?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, we never provided such an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And finally, can we go to the -- almost the last page of this document, penultimate, number 11, page 11. Item number 4: "The secret procedure for transferring and receiving orders to implement tasks ..." Can we pause there. Do you agree that says "orders"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: It does say "order," yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "To implement tasks, measures, or other activities ... shall be established subsequently. " Were you ever given a secret procedure?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was never given any kind of secret procedure nor am I aware that such a measure was ever adopted within the party. I don't know of anything like that at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's all I ask about the document. May that be admitted as an exhibit now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P69, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want you briefly, please, to look at 65 ter 00097. Which is the same as 1598, apparently. All right. That's -- that's jumping ahead slightly in the chronology, but it's because it's dated on the last second page the 26th of April, but it's headed "The Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, extract from the instructions from the work of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people." And if we go to the second page now of the document. Dated, as I say, the 26th of April, 1992. And is signed by Mr. Djeric. Well, I say signed. It bears his typed signature. Did you receive this document, Mr. Djekanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: Looking at it from this point of view today, I have the impression that I'm seeing it for the first time. I cannot remember precisely whether I had it then or not, whether I saw it or not. I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, seeing it for the first time can't be right, can it, because you were shown it in an interview.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: The reason for that is that the document could have gone through the Kotor Varos municipal Executive Board and not through the party Executive Board, and that is the reason why I'm saying that I may not have seen it. I'm not disputing the document's existence. Perhaps in this form or some other form.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, all I wanted to ask you about is item number 14: "The Crisis Staff shall ... make decisions --" Sorry, paragraph 14: "The Crisis Staff shall ... make decisions and hold sessions in --" sorry. Thank you. "The Crisis Staff shall convene and make decisions in the presence of all its members, take official minutes, issue written decisions, and submit weekly reports to the regional and state organisations of the Serbian republic ..." All I want to ask you is, did you have minutes taken of your meetings?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: When the Crisis Staff was functioning, we did take minutes. The bulk of the excerpts from those minutes you also have, so the question is superfluous. We did have meetings -- minutes, not only at the Crisis Staff meetings but only -- but at all types of meetings or sessions. We did take the minutes of the meetings. There were transcripts of those sessions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you submit weekly reports to the regional and state organisations?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELKO DJEKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the period that this refers to or could refer to, many communications had broken down in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So now I can decisively state that the organs at the central of the party did not receive reports that were submitted by us. Sometimes we would give them a summary that would be those from the meetings at the regional Crisis Staff sessions, but we did not make reports for each individual meeting. This was simply something that was done from case to case, just as if -- as the change -- as there were changes in the need for convening Crisis Staff meetings. Sometimes they would be held from time to time. Sometimes there was need for them to be held on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Honestly, sir, I'm going to ask you again --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Please just answer the question I ask and don't volunteer information that really isn't necessary. Right. I want to move, please, to the -- or go back, rather, because that was later on, and look at document 65 ter 671, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
